land.text: Birgi, Ephesus and the Maeander valley, held by Mehmed Bey, 'originally a vassal of the Germiyanids'

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Founded/split from the Germiyanids: 1308'; Ephesus was captured in October 1304 (Aydinids page) while Mehmed was still a Germiyanid vassal.

land.text: the Aydinid lands, annexed by the Ottoman Empire in 1426 (infobox)

successors.note: The Anatolian beyliks table gives 1300-1425; the Aydinids infobox 1426. Cliopatria's Ottoman shape takes the land in 1429.

capitals.name: Birgi (later Ayasluğ, Selçuk)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Birgi Selçuk'; the Anatolian beyliks table: 'Birgi, later Ayasluğ (Selçuk)'. Neither page dates the move to Ayasluğ, so Birgi is carried for the whole life (confidence 1 on the split); Ayasluğ (Selçuk, the site of Ephesus) is about 37.95 N, 27.37 E.

rulers.name: Umur
rulers.note: Table 1334-1348; the Smyrniote crusades infobox has Umur Bey 1343-1348 and Hızır Beg 1348-1351.

rulers.name: Junayd (Cüneyd) of Aydın
rulers.note: The infobox calls him 'İzmiroğlu Cüneyd Bey'.

correction.text: the 1305 shape plus the capital Birgi, valid 1308-1325

keyframe_review.note: The infobox dates the beylik 'Founded/split from the Germiyanids: 1308' ('before being killed in 1308, which caused Mehmed to declare his independence from the Germiyanids'), so the shape holds from 1308; 1305-1307 is Mehmed Bey's holding as a Germiyanid vassal after he 'captured the city of Ephesus in October 1304' (not drawn as a state). 7,982 km2 (27 cells) round Aydın and Ephesus; the capital Birgi (just beyond its northern edge) is added as a 25 km disc. No infobox area on the page.

correction.text: the 1326 shape plus Birgi, valid 1326-1328; Smyrna contested

keyframe_review.note: Years only: the 1326 shape (7,958 km2, 25 km2 less than 1305, grid noise) plus Birgi, valid 1326-1328 while Smyrna is besieged ('From 1317–1329, the Aydinids besieged Smyrna.').

correction.text: the 1326 shape plus Birgi and Smyrna, valid 1329-1343

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Smyrna was 'conquered by the Aydinids at the beginning of the 14th century' and used 1326-1329 as a base for piracy (Smyrniote crusades page); the Aydinids page ends the siege in 1329. Cliopatria's Aydin shape stops 40 km short of İzmir, so the city is added with a 20 km disc for 1329-1343.

correction.text: the 1326 shape plus Birgi, valid 1344-1389; Smyrna in Latin hands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the crusaders surprised Smyrna and retook the harbour fortress and harbour in 1344 (the acropolis held out), Smyrna remained in Latin hands until the Timurid siege of 1402 (Smyrniote crusades page); the Aydinids page gives 1348 for the conquest by the crusader coalition. The shape returns to the 1326 shape plus Birgi for 1344-1389.

correction.text: the restored beylik: the 1326 shape plus Birgi, valid 1402-1414

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's 1326 shape runs to 1414 and ignores the Ottoman interval, but the ruler table has 'Ottoman rule | 1390–1402' and 'İsaoğlu Musa Bey | 1402–1403'; Bayezid I 'conquered the beyliks of Aydin, Saruhan and Menteshe' in 1390. The restored beylik is drawn as the old core plus Birgi for 1402-1414; the page gives no extent after 1402 and does not say whether Smyrna returned.
The 1415 shape (7,736 km2, 221 km2 less than 1326; one cell at the southern edge) plus Birgi for 1415-1421. No page explains the 1415 change; grid noise. Cüneyd rules 1405-1426 (table).

The 1422 shape (7,736 km2, as 1415) plus Birgi, valid 1422-1426. Cliopatria runs it to 1428; the infobox ends the beylik by 'annexation into the Ottoman Empire: 1426' and Cüneyd's reign to 1426 (the Anatolian beyliks table: 1300-1425). Cliopatria's Ottoman shape takes the land in 1429.

region.text: Birgi and Ephesus with the lower Maeander valley

ledger.note: 1308: Mehmed Bey declares the independence of the Aydinid beylik at Birgi. Infobox 'Founded/split from the Germiyanids: 1308'; 'before being killed in 1308, which caused Mehmed to declare his independence from the Germiyanids'; he had 'captured the city of Ephesus in October 1304'. The year is the page's; the land (Ephesus, the Maeander valley, Birgi) is the reading of the capital and Cliopatria's shape.

ledger.counterpart: defenders of Smyrna (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1317: the Aydinids begin the siege of Smyrna. 'From 1317–1329, the Aydinids besieged Smyrna.' The page does not name the defenders.

ledger.counterpart: defenders of Smyrna (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1329: the siege of Smyrna ends in Aydinid hands. 'From 1317–1329, the Aydinids besieged Smyrna'; the Smyrniote crusades page has the city 'conquered by the Aydinids at the beginning of the 14th century' and used 1326-1329 as a base for piracy, so the two pages disagree on when the city fell.

ledger.counterpart: defenders of Smyrna (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1329: Smyrna is held by the Aydinids. Smyrniote crusades page: 'conquered by the Aydinids at the beginning of the 14th century' and used from 1326 to 1329 as a pirate base; the Aydinids page ends the siege in 1329. The earlier holder is not named on either page (confidence 2 for the year and the place, the counterpart is the unnamed defenders).

region.text: the harbour of Smyrna and its fortress

ledger.note: 1344: the crusader fleet takes the harbour fortress of Smyrna. The Smyrniote crusades page: after the victory at Pallene (13 May 1344) the crusaders surprised Smyrna later in 1344 and retook the harbour fortress and harbour at the first assault, but not the acropolis; on 17 January 1345 Umur Bey attacked the crusaders at mass and killed the patriarch Henry of Asti, Martino Zaccaria and Pietro Zeno. The Aydinids page puts the conquest in 1348.
1390: Bayezid I conquers Aydın. 'In a single campaign over the summer and fall of 1390, Bayezid conquered the beyliks of Aydin, Saruhan and Menteshe.' The ruler table has 'Ottoman rule | 1390–1402'.

1402: the Aydinid beylik is restored. The ruler table resumes with 'İsaoğlu Musa Bey | 1402–1403' after 'Ottoman rule | 1390–1402'; the Bayezid I page has Bayezid defeated at Ankara on 20 July 1402 and 'many beyliks regained their independence' (no year). The Aydinids page does not name Timur.
1426: the Ottomans annex the Aydinid lands. Infobox 'Ended by annexation into the Ottoman Empire: 1426' and Junayd's reign to 1426 in the table; the Anatolian beyliks table gives 1300-1425.
1426: the Aydinid beylik ends. Infobox 'Ended by annexation into the Ottoman Empire: 1426'; 'Succeeded by: Ottoman Empire'.

wars.name: Aydinid siege of Smyrna
belligerents: defenders of Smyrna (not named on the page)
wars.outcome: The Aydinids besiege Smyrna from 1317 to 1329 and hold it as a pirate base from 1326 to 1329.
wars.note: The Smyrniote crusades page has the city conquered 'at the beginning of the 14th century'; the pages disagree and name no defender.

wars.name: Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347 (Aydinid intervention)
wars.outcome: The Aydinids under Umur 'participated in the Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347'; the page names no territorial result.
wars.note: 'In 1332 and 1333 Umur launched piratical raids across the Aegean' (same page).

wars.name: Smyrniote crusades
wars.outcome: The allied fleet beat the Turkish fleet at Pallene on 13 May 1344; the crusaders took the harbour fortress of Smyrna later in 1344 but not the acropolis; Umur Bey killed the patriarch and two leaders on 17 January 1345; a second crusade under Humbert II won at Mytilene in February 1346; Smyrna stayed in Latin hands until the Timurid siege of 1402.
wars.note: The Aydinids page has the crusader conquest in 1348.

wars.name: Bayezid I's conquest of Aydın, Saruhan and Menteshe
wars.outcome: Aydın is held by the Ottomans from 1390 to 1402; the Aydinids return under Timur's defeat of Bayezid at Ankara in 1402.
wars.note: 'In a single campaign over the summer and fall of 1390, Bayezid conquered the beyliks of Aydin, Saruhan and Menteshe.'

certainty.note: No page opened gives a treaty line or a survey; the beylik's frontiers with Menteshe, Saruhan, Germiyan and the Byzantines are approximate throughout.

notes:
Row identity: Cliopatria's 'Beylik of Aydin' (Wikipedia 'Aydinids', Q717112) is one state, 1308-1426 on its page. The Cliopatria row (1305-1428) is a 27-cell shape round Aydın and Ephesus; it lacks Birgi, the capital, and Smyrna (İzmir), so each verdict adds a 25 km disc round Birgi (lon 28.065, lat 38.255; Birgi is not in places.jsonl, gazetteer name needed) and, for 1329-1343, a 20 km disc round İzmir.
Dates: the page gives 'Founded/split from the Germiyanids: 1308' and ends the state by annexation in 1426 (the Anatolian beyliks table says 1300-1425). Cliopatria begins in 1305 and ends in 1428; the 1305-1307 years are Mehmed Bey's Germiyanid-vassal holding (Ephesus taken in October 1304) and are not drawn here; the germiyanids dossier has no event for them. No infobox area exists on any page, so no ratio.
Page budget (up to 5): Aydinids, Smyrniote crusades, Anatolian beyliks, Bayezid I; two more pages (Ottoman Interregnum, Mehmed I) were opened for Cüneyd and the 1413-1426 Ottoman campaigns and said nothing on Aydın, so the end (1426 or 1425) rests on the infobox and one table row. The Ottoman reincorporation by Murad II (1425/1426) is on no page opened.
Disagreements: Smyrna (conquered 'at the beginning of the 14th century' on the Smyrniote crusades page against besieged 1317-1329 on the Aydinids page; crusader conquest 1344 against 1348); the ruler dates of Umur (table 1334-1348, crusades infobox 1343-1348). The earlier holders of Smyrna are named on no page (counterpart is a text string), and the crusader coalition 1344-1374 has no dossier (the hospitaller-rhodes dossier uses the same string 'Crusade of 1344 (holders of Smyrna)' for its 1374 gain).
Cross-dossier: the ottoman-empire dossier has no gain for Aydin in 1390 and no loss in 1402 except its general 1402 line ('Anatolian beyliks restored by Timur') and has no 1426 gain (its Cliopatria shape adds the land in 1429); beylik-of-menteshe and beylik-of-saruhan carry the same 1390/1402 pairs. A Hospitaller or Genoese counterpart for Ephesus in the 1340s-1350s is on no page opened (the neighbours list shows republic-of-genoa touching 1352-1428).
